I sped up the workload by changing the equality check in `maybe_cast_to_integer_array` in `pandas/core/dtypes/cast.py`. The best of 30 runs is now about 0.67 ms per call. I didn't time the original, so I can't give a before/after figure. In the earlier profile, the `np.array_equal` call was about half of the workload's time.

For float input arrays, the check now casts the integer result back to the input's float dtype and compares that with the input. That avoids upcasting a float32 array and an int32 array to float64 for the comparison. Other input types still use `np.array_equal`.

I ran `pandas/tests/dtypes/test_common.py` and `pandas/tests/series/test_constructors.py`, but the output I saw was cut off and showed only warnings. I can't confirm they passed.

I also didn't run the full 1000-repeat workload script.
